newsitem.title: UK: PPL trials new cystic fibrosis treatment.
newsitem.headline: PPL trials new cystic fibrosis treatment.

text.p: Britain's PPL Therapeutics Plc said on Thursday it had started Phase 1 clinical trials on humans for a potential new treatment for cystic fibrosis.
The compound, alpha-1-antitrypsin, will be administered to 40 healthy volunteers to confirm its safety for humans. The study will take place in the UK and will take two months to complete.
The Scottish genetics and proteins specialist said the compound addressed the fundamental problems of lung tissue breakdown in cystic fibrosis, which is not tackled by existing treatment.

Managing director Ron James said alpha-1-antitrypsin, the company's lead compound, was the first example of the group's transgenic technology, which will make many new treatments possible based on complex human proteins. These would otherwise not be available or would be too expensive for widespread use, he said. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
